findings.summary: A conflict-style config block is dropped into the Range Syntax section, six pages before conflicts, markers, or the BASE section exist.
findings.evidence: Directly under the "5. Range Syntax" table: "git config merge.conflictStyle zdiff3" / "# adds the ||||||| base section" / "# set --global; never guess intent again"
findings.fix: Delete this code block from page 1 and place it on page 7 next to "2. Marker Anatomy" / "3. The Labels Invert", where `|||||||`, base text, and "guessing intent" have already been defined.

findings.summary: The fast-forward page closes with a three-way-merge argument that relies on BASE, a term not defined until page 3.
findings.evidence: "Two-way diff cannot do this: without BASE, 'they added a line' and 'we deleted a line' look identical. BASE supplies intent."
findings.fix: Move this paragraph to page 3, immediately after the "2. The Three Inputs" table that defines BASE/OURS/THEIRS, and give "this" an explicit antecedent ("Three-way merge needs BASE: ...").

findings.summary: The rename-threshold tuning flag `-M` does not exist for `git merge`; merge/ort rename detection is tuned with the strategy option `-X find-renames=<n>`.
findings.evidence: Page 3, section "6. Renames Are Inferred": "Default threshold 50%; tune with -M (e.g. -M40%)" — stated on the three-way-merge/ort page, where a reader will run `git merge -M40% feature` and get "error: unknown option". `-M` is a diff-family option (git diff/log/format-patch); git-merge-strategies documents `find-renames[=<n>]` (with `rename-threshold=<n>` as a deprecated synonym) as the ort/recursive option.
findings.fix: Change the bullet to "Default threshold 50%; tune with -X find-renames=40% on merge/rebase (-M40% on diff/log)".

findings.summary: Rebase section 1's bullets are separated from their heading and example by two unrelated three-way-merge blocks, so page 4 opens with headless rebase content.
findings.evidence: Page 3 ends with heading "1. What It Computes" + "git rebase main   # replays main..feature"; page 4 then opens with "7. Strategy Options" and the "Cost Model" callout before the matching bullets "Take the commits in `main..feature`".
findings.fix: Keep the merge leftovers ("7. Strategy Options", "Cost Model") on page 3 and start page 4 with the "1. What It Computes" heading, code, and bullets as one contiguous block.

findings.summary: Cherry-pick commands and the sentence explaining why cherry-picks conflict appear before cherry-pick is introduced and before the table that supplies the explanation.
findings.evidence: Page 4 ends with "git cherry-pick 9f2a1c      # one commit" and "That is exactly why a cherry-pick can conflict — it is never a blind patch application." — while "1. Rebase's Atom" and the "2. It Is A Three-Way Merge" table (BASE = C's parent, OURS = HEAD, THEIRS = C) are on page 5.
findings.fix: Move the cherry-pick code block and that paragraph to page 5, placing the paragraph directly after the BASE/OURS/THEIRS table it refers back to.

findings.summary: The conflicts page ends with the merge-vs-rebase conclusion, whose pronoun "both" has no antecedent on that page.
findings.evidence: "With no conflicts both give the same tree. The entire difference is recorded history, not shipped code."
findings.fix: Move this paragraph to page 8, directly after the two "Axis | Merge | Rebase" tables (whose last row is "final tree | identical | identical"), so "both" refers to the compared operations.

findings.summary: The Golden Rule callout claims its corollaries are on the same page, but every corollary — and the flags used in the code block beneath it — is on page 9.
findings.evidence: "Never rebase commits that exist outside your repository and that others may have built work on. Everything else on this page is a corollary." followed by "git push --force-with-lease \\" / "  --force-if-includes origin feature", while "1. Why Push Breaks" and "2. Force Flags Ranked" are on page 9.
findings.fix: Move the Golden Rule callout and the force-push code block to the top of page 9, above "1. Why Push Breaks", and change "this page" to "the rest of this page" there; if the callout must stay on page 8, drop the code block and reword to "everything on the next page is a corollary".

findings.summary: The flat "~90 days" reflog retention figure is wrong for exactly the entries the handbook later relies on for rebase recovery — unreachable entries expire after 30 days by default.
findings.evidence: Page 1: "Kept ~90 days; entries addressable as HEAD@{n}", relied on by page 4's "Old commits become unreachable, not modified / They live in the reflog until it expires". gc.reflogExpire defaults to 90 days but applies to reachable entries; gc.reflogExpireUnreachable defaults to 30 days and covers entries created by rebase/amend — i.e. the pre-rebase tips.
findings.fix: Amend to "Kept ~90 days (gc.reflogExpire); entries whose commits are unreachable — e.g. pre-rebase tips — only ~30 days (gc.reflogExpireUnreachable)".

findings.summary: "A branch is a 41-byte file" is presented as the definition of a ref, but refs are routinely stored in packed-refs (or the reftable backend), where no such file exists.
findings.evidence: Page 1: "A branch is a 41-byte file holding one SHA" plus "$ cat .git/refs/heads/main", and page 3's sidebox "Before: cat .git/refs/heads/main … After: same file, new SHA / That is the entire operation". After any `git gc` (including auto-gc) the loose ref is removed and `cat .git/refs/heads/main` fails with "No such file or directory"; reftable repos have no `.git/refs` files at all.
findings.fix: Add a qualifier — "a loose ref is a 41-byte file; once packed it lives in .git/packed-refs — use `git rev-parse main` / `git update-ref` to read or write it portably" — and use `git rev-parse main` in the page-3 sidebox.

findings.summary: A patch-id consequence is filed as the last bullet of the Revert section, where it does not follow from anything in that list.
findings.evidence: Under "7. Revert: The Inverse": "Applies the reverse diff as a NEW commit" / "Adds history instead of rewriting it" / "Therefore safe on shared branches" / "Re-rebasing a merged branch is usually a no-op"
findings.fix: Move "Re-rebasing a merged branch is usually a no-op" into section "5. Patch-ID", after "Rebase drops picks whose patch-id is upstream".

findings.summary: The marker diagram says the `|||||||` base section is "diff3 only", contradicting page 1, which tells the reader to set zdiff3 precisely to get that section.
findings.evidence: Page 7: "||||||| merged ancestor   # diff3 only" vs page 1: "git config merge.conflictStyle zdiff3 / # adds the ||||||| base section". Both `diff3` and `zdiff3` emit the base section; only the plain `merge` style omits it.
findings.fix: Change the comment to "# diff3 / zdiff3 styles only".
